subject: Aggregation policy exception: short-term p95 measurement adjustment
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Amira Hassan <amira@stellarmeds.com>, ops@stellarmeds.com
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Aggregation policy exception: short-term p95 measurement adjustment

Team —

Quick background: StellarMed (clinical SaaS, onboarding next week) is asking for a temporary tweak to how we measure p95 for their hosted API. They saw a number of short, large bursts during a recent integration test (attached logs) that pushed the measured p95 well above the committed target despite median latency being within our normal range. Their go-live is scheduled for 9/08 and procurement wants a concise, time-limited exception so their internal stakeholders will sign the order.

Request: They asked if we can exclude a small class of startup bursts from the p95 window for 60 days while they roll out client-side batching and rate smoothing. Proposed safe approach below; want product and reliability alignment before I confirm with them.

Proposed temporary policy (business-sensible, low-risk):
- Window adjustment: measure p50 across current 1-minute sampling; for p95 only, apply a 60-minute rolling aggregation with a burst-isolation carveout that excludes contiguous short-duration spikes when they are traceable to external deployment events (max 3 minutes per spike).
- Timebox: 60 days from approval, auto-expiry unless extended by signed addendum.
- Guardrails: limit to a single customer IP range per approval; automatic anomaly detection that will suspend exception if error rates or sustained latency increase across region.
- Evidence: StellarMed provided velocity logs (attached) and a client rollout plan.

Can you weigh in on feasibility and operational risk? Karthik — does this break any metric tooling assumptions? Marissa — is this something we can instrument and monitor with auto-suspension? Ben — if we can do this, I need a short note I can send Amira confirming the time limit and the technical guardrails.

Thanks,
Kim
Kimberly Park
Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
attachments: [stellarmed_velocity_logs.csv (CSV, 2.1 MB), sla_exception_form_filled.pdf (PDF, 320 KB)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Aggregation policy exception: short-term p95 measurement adjustment

Kim —

Thanks for the clear ask and the logs. High level: changing the p95 measurement aggregation is doable, but it has several implications:

1) Metric semantics: Our SLAs are computed by the metrics pipeline which expects fixed-window aggregation for p95 (1-5 minute buckets depending on route). Switching to a 60-minute rolling window for a single customer will require a per-customer override and additional downstream labeling so we don't contaminate global aggregates.

2) Alerting & billing: Alerts and internal dashboards will need to respect the exception. Billing should remain unchanged (we don't want to appear to be modifying billing metrics), but legal needs the carveout language.

3) Complexity: Implementation would be a short-lived feature flag + a label on the request path. Runtime risk is low if we can gate by customer_id and IP range, but testing is required. Estimated work: 2 sprint-days of dev + 1 day QA + a small infra config change to the metrics service.

If we adopt Kim's guardrails (timebox + auto-suspend on sustained anomalies), I think this is acceptable. I can scope the minimal change set and flag the metrics pipelines team.

Karthik
Principal Product Manager — Serving Runtime

Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Aggregation policy exception: short-term p95 measurement adjustment

Kim / Karthik —

Operational notes from SRE POV:

- We can implement an "exception label" that the metrics pipeline honors; it would route the labeled samples to a separate aggregation path to compute the p95 variant. This is preferable to mutating global behavior.
- Auto-suspend: we can add a guard that revokes the label if the exceptional customer's error rate goes above 1.5% for 10 minutes, or if region-wide tail latency increases. That logic exists in our canary tooling.
- Observability: we'll need a small dashboard tile that shows both the standard p95 and the alternate p95-with-carveout to make tradeoffs visible.
- Rollout: feature-flag the labeling and test against a staging copy of StellarMed's traffic first.

Implementation estimate: 3 engineering-days (SRE + metrics engineers) to deliver a conservative, auditable path plus the dashboard. Testing required before we sign anything.

I'm fine with a 60-day timebox. We should also require StellarMed to sign the exception addendum that states they will implement client-side smoothing within that window.

Marissa
Head of Reliability — Redwood Inference

Amira —

Thanks for sending the logs and the signed request form. We've reviewed this with Product and Reliability and can support a narrowly scoped, temporary measurement exception for StellarMed under the following conditions (please confirm acceptance in reply):

1) Scope: Applies only to API key(s) associated with StellarMed account 4729 and the IP ranges listed in the request form.
2) Behavior: For 60 days from the effective date, our metrics pipeline will compute the contract p95 using an alternate aggregation that applies a 60-minute rolling window and excludes isolated spikes shorter than 3 minutes if they correlate with deployment events.
3) Guardrails: The exception is automatically suspended if error rate > 1.5% for 10 continuous minutes, or if we detect a region-wide performance regression.
4) Audit & visibility: We'll provide a dashboard link showing both standard p95 and the adjusted p95 daily; Redwood retains the right to revoke the exception if safeguards trip.
5) Legal: Final approval requires a signed addendum appended to the Master Services Agreement confirming the 60-day timebox and the limited scope.

If you accept, please reply to this thread and upload the signed addendum to the Drive folder linked below. Once we have that, we'll schedule a controlled staging test and target going live with the exception within 3 business days.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Stellarmed-SLO-Evidence

Looking forward —
